subject: Banking
title: Student Loan Servicing
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Student Loan Servicing.

hook.text: US student loan debt is $1.7 trillion. Banks and loan servicers earn billions managing payments on degrees already.

buildup.text: Loan servicers collect payments, manage accounts, and process forgiveness applications.

discovery.text: Private student loans charge 4-14% interest. Unlike mortgages, student debt cannot be discharged in bankruptcy.

twist.text: Government-backed student loans are risk-free for servicers.

climax.text: Student loan servicing is banking's safest revenue. Guaranteed income, no risk, and a borrower who can't walk away.

punchline.text: $1.7 trillion in debt you can't escape. Student loans are risk-free for banks.

quiz.question: What makes student loan debt unique?
options: It generally cannot be discharged in bankruptcy

details.summary: Banks and their affiliated servicers profit from student loan servicing by earning per-borrower monthly fees, late charges, and penalties. The incentive structure rewards minimizing costs per borrower rather than helping borrowers find the cheapest repayment options.
details.whyItMatters: Over 43 million Americans carry student debt, and servicer incentives directly affect their financial lives. When servicers profit from confusion rather than clarity, borrowers pay thousands more than necessary.
takeaways: Servicers earn a fixed monthly fee per borrower regardless of service quality
Per-borrower fees create incentives to minimize time spent on each account
Pushing borrowers to forbearance is faster and cheaper than enrolling in income-driven plans

faq.question: How do student loan servicers make money?
faq.answer: Servicers receive a monthly fee per borrower, typically $1-3 for current loans and up to $5 for delinquent accounts. Since the fee is fixed, servicers maximize profit by spending as little time as possible on each borrower, discouraging complex repayment assistance.

faq.question: Why do servicers push forbearance instead of income-driven repayment?
faq.answer: Processing a forbearance request takes minutes while enrolling a borrower in income-driven repayment requires collecting documentation and takes much longer. Since the per-borrower payment is the same regardless, servicers profit more from the quicker option.
